name: Ironbloom Annex — Chrome Sculpture Garden
creator: Vasile Nkemdirim and the Ironbloom Annex Collective
description: A half-acre open-air sculpture garden installed without permission on a derelict lot in Tier 2's Pilsen-Moksha district, featuring over two hundred chrome and salvaged-augmentation sculptures created by augmented artists celebrating their own cyberware as aesthetic objects. The sculptures range from intimate hand-sized pieces to a central fifteen-meter tower constructed entirely from donated and salvaged limb augmentations welded into a branching form. The garden has been demolished and rebuilt three times after corponation property disputes.
medium: physical sculpture, chrome and salvaged augmentation components
cultural_impact: Became the spiritual home of the broader Ironbloom chrome pride movement and one of the most visited unsanctioned cultural spaces in GLMZ; the tower, called 'The Ancestor,' has become an informal memorial for augmentation-related workplace deaths.
controversy: HelixCorp's augmentation division claims ownership of several component parts in the sculptures as proprietary hardware; a class-action countersuit argues that augmentations removed from living bodies revert to personal property.
story_hooks: Someone is stripping sculptures from the garden at night — not for theft, but apparently searching for a specific augmentation component hidden somewhere in the collection.
The Ancestor tower is scheduled for demolition under a new corponation easement, and the collective has seventy-two hours to either move it or defend it.
A sculpture in the garden is identified as containing the chrome arm of a person officially listed as alive — but no one has seen them in four years.
